steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Relief printing (linocut, woodcut) cuts away negative space; the raised surface is inked and printed.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Intaglio (drypoint, etching) holds ink in incised lines below the surface; the plate surface is wiped clean.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Screen printing forces ink through a mesh stencil; monoprinting creates one unique print from a painted surface.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Editioning means producing multiple identical prints; registration ensures colours align in multi-plate prints.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring printmaking techniques. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with printmaking techniques. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with printmaking techniques. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to printmaking techniques, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes. | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
